subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own only runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, or should core own the full temp artifact registry and janitor classification model requested here?
rationale: The current request spans core runtime safety, agent harness APIs, cleanup policy, storage design, and plugin workflow ownership, and repository policy does not make that product boundary automatic.

options.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
options.body: Implement durable runtime checks and a small SQLite-backed provenance API, then leave review/audit workflow classification to plugins or ClawHub unless the seam proves insufficient.

options.title: Full core artifact registry
options.body: Make core own artifact classes, provenance storage, durable promotion, and janitor semantics for OpenClaw-created temp files.

options.title: Track only concrete temp-path bugs
options.body: Decline the broad model and handle future temp-backed runtime or data-loss reports as narrower doctor/runtime fixes.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
recommendation.body: Implement durable runtime checks and a small SQLite-backed provenance API, then leave review/audit workflow classification to plugins or ClawHub unless the seam proves insufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal across product scope, ClawHub routing, filesystem safety, daemon path checks, and doctor-adjacent work.
